correctness.rationale: In attack-topological order each head sees only decided predecessors, so the recursion has an order-independent solution K and its attack targets are exactly A minus K. For a complete E, inductively a head rejected by K is attacked by E through the same accepted tail; each tail of an accepted head contains a rejected predecessor, already attacked by E, so E attacks any closed attacker of this head. Completeness forces acceptance. Stability forces the same membership recursion directly. When K is closed, it defends each member by attacking an outsider in each attacking tail; for a rejected head a firing tail T has closed attacker cl_S(T) contained in K, which conflict-freeness prevents K from attacking. This proves all three families are {K} or empty, even with empty or cyclic supports and also for A empty. The algorithm needs only an attack incidence-list topological sort, a head-indexed attack-rule scan, and a scan of the original support rules; no support closure search is needed. A violated rule supplies the claimed witness in the stated linear bound. value.rationale: A natural tractable fragment of collective argumentation is characterized by a condition on attacks alone; supports may still be cyclic. The single linear-time existence test and explicit failure witness replace general closed-attacker/extension searches and isolate the obstruction to complete and grounded existence. The preferred counterexample prevents an overgeneralization to all semantics.
